items.title: Hafnia Q3 net profit $170.8m; plans TORM share dividend
items.summary: Hafnia earned $170.8m in Q3 2026 ($0.34/share) on an average fleet TCE of $32,708/day, with nine-month profit at $628.3m. The board intends to hand out all 20.36m TORM shares (about $686.6m at the Nov 17 close) as an extraordinary dividend in place of Q3–Q4 cash payouts; Q4 is 74% fixed at $55,148/day as of Nov 13.

items.title: Clean tanker spot earnings slip 4.8% on the week
items.summary: Makai Marine's Week 47 report puts clean spot earnings down 4.8% week on week and 13.4% below the late-October peak, with Atlantic MRs accounting for most of the decline as softer US Gulf arbitrage and ballaster incentives loosened balances. LRs eased 2.1%, Pacific MRs held steady and Handies were the only size to gain.

items.title: Middle East MR rates down w125 as Hormuz transits slow
items.summary: Platts assessed the benchmark Middle East MR route w125 lower on Nov 18; Vitol put Torm Stellar on subjects at w500 for a Nov 25 Duqm–East Africa diesel cargo. S&P Global data show daily Hormuz transits at 14 on Nov 9 versus 32 at end-October, and the PG–North Asia LR1 benchmark has not risen day on day for almost a month.

items.title: Hanwha Philly cuts steel on first of four Jones Act MRs
items.summary: Construction began Nov 17 on four 49,500 dwt MR product/chemical tankers for Hanwha Shipping, built to Jones Act rules and IMO Type 2/3 chemical standards, with an optional 18-segregation layout. Deliveries are planned for 2029–2030; Hanwha calls it the first US-built MR program in nearly a decade.

items.title: Suezmaxes and Aframaxes take a bigger share of Hormuz flows
items.summary: Vortexa data show Suezmaxes and Aframaxes moved more than 2m b/d through Hormuz in October, a wartime high, as total Gulf exports reached 11.4m b/d. VLCCs had made up 72% of transits (BRS); Suezmax Gulf–China freight is running at roughly one-third to just under half of the VLCC rate on that route.

items.title: Court ruling clouds license for Texas GulfLink export terminal
items.summary: A 5th Circuit decision voiding MARAD's approval of Sentinel Midstream's $2.1bn Texas GulfLink (about 30 miles off Freeport, designed for ~2m b/d) took effect Oct 30. Opponents say the license must now be suspended; Sentinel says it remains valid, still targets Q4 2028 start-up and plans a Supreme Court petition.

items.title: IMO tallies $10.5bn in maritime climate finance for 2018–2023
items.summary: An IMO study released Nov 19 found $10.5bn of direct maritime climate finance over six years, about 0.14% of global climate finance, rising to $4.7bn in 2023. Ports took 39% and alternative fuels 24%; the report puts shipping's decarbonisation capital need at $1.2–1.6 trillion by 2050, ahead of the Nov 23–27 GHG working group and MEPC 85.

items.title: Tanker struck 8 nm north of Khasab; Hormuz traffic about 65% below normal
items.summary: An outbound tanker was hit by a projectile on its port bow around 1500 UTC Friday, causing a fire but no reported casualties (UKMTO Warning 214-26). UKMTO's weekly count shows 115 outbound and 148 inbound transits, down from 139 and 169 the week before; NAVIG8 MESSI, struck Nov 17, is under tow with one crew missing and 11 injured, per ADNOC.

items.title: Houthis tell ships to leave Saudi Red Sea ports after Hodeidah strikes
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it struck Hodeidah port on Friday; Yemen's information minister says the port is still operating. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree told shipping companies to move vessels out of Saudi Red Sea ports and warned airlines away from Saudi airspace.

items.title: Two ships sink in Bulgaria's Black Sea EEZ; all 31 crew rescued
items.summary: The general cargo ship BETUL 8 sank on Nov 16 and the LPG tanker GAS HUSKY on Nov 17, both inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. Ambrey counts six vessels struck in the Black Sea since Nov 13; causes were not detailed in the report.

items.title: LPG carrier TARA GAS still burning and adrift off Oman
items.summary: The Panama-flagged LPG tanker, first hit Nov 16 about 7 nm north of Khasab and set on fire in a second strike Nov 17, was drifting about 5.7 nm off Khawr Ghub Ali on Nov 18; 24 of 25 crew were rescued and one is missing. Vanguard Tech identifies the ADNOC L&S vessel attacked the same evening (1 missing, 11 injured) as product tanker NAVIG8 MESSI; ADNOC has not named it.

items.title: Houston pilot indicted over 2024 Ship Channel collision
items.summary: Pilot Darris Jefferson faces a federal seaman's manslaughter charge over the July 2024 collision near Lynchburg in which the bulker Yangze 7 struck the towboat Miss Peggy, which sank with one deckhand killed. The NTSB cited a 39-minute non-operational phone call; the allegations are unproven and his first court appearance is Nov 24.

items.title: LA/Long Beach security workers' contract expires Nov 21
items.summary: About 250 ILWU Local 26 security workers could walk out from 12:01 a.m. Saturday; they staff six terminals handling about 85% of Long Beach and 33% of Los Angeles cargo. The PMA has offered a $3,200 one-time bonus, and talks were set to resume Friday, Nov 20.

items.title: Bulker MIRO G grounds on French Atlantic coast
items.summary: The Maltese-flag Handysize MIRO G (28,200 dwt), in ballast for Rouen to load wheat for Libya, dragged anchor in 48-knot gusts and grounded near Lit-et-Mixe shortly after midnight Friday. A military helicopter lifted 19 of 22 crew; more than 100 t of diesel is aboard and no pollution had been detected.

items.title: Stocks fall a sixth session: S&P 500 −2% to 7,175.83 (Nov 19)
items.summary: Thursday's close: S&P 500 −147.80 (−2.0%) at 7,175.83, Dow −1,101.11 (−2.2%) at 49,097.06, Nasdaq −550.69 (−2.3%) at 23,879.20. AP attributed the drop to continued selling in AI-related stocks; the S&P 500 is 8.2% below last month's record and down 5.1% for the week so far.

items.title: Friday midday: S&P 500 −1.4%, Nasdaq −2.5% as chip stocks fall
items.summary: As of 11:08 a.m. ET on Nov 20, the S&P 500 was down 1.4% (on track for a seventh straight loss), the Nasdaq 2.5% and the Dow 18 points. Nvidia was off 6%, AMD 9.4% and Broadcom 9.2%; Anthropic traded at $86.83, below Thursday's close but above its $83 IPO price. These are intraday figures, not closes.

items.title: Brent settles at $91.98, WTI at $83.21 (Nov 19)
items.summary: Brent finished +0.03% at $91.98 and WTI −0.06% at $83.21, WTI's lowest since Aug 26, as Hormuz tanker reports offset surplus concerns. Gold fell 3.04% to $3,628.30 on a firmer dollar. A Nov 19 Henry Hub settlement was not available in the sources reviewed.

items.title: 10-year yield eases to 4.95% Friday; December hike still priced
items.summary: AP put the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% late Friday morning, from 5.04% late Thursday, as investors moved toward bonds. Reuters reported CME FedWatch showing a quarter-point hike at the December FOMC as essentially fully priced; the dollar index was 103.86 in Asian trade.

items.title: Michigan sentiment 51.5; Philly Fed falls to 6.3
items.summary: The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0 in October (released Nov 20). On Nov 19 the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index dropped to 6.3 from 20.9 and initial jobless claims were 203,000.

items.title: Asian stocks post worst week since March 2020
items.summary: On Nov 20 MSCI's Asia-Pacific index fell 2.5%, leaving it down about 7% for the week. Japan's Nikkei lost 4.1% (6.8% for the week) and South Korea's KOSPI 4.7% (7.5% for the week), led by technology shares.

items.title: Walmart raises outlook; Gap gains on Q3 sales
items.summary: Walmart reported Q3 revenue up 5.2% to $188.8bn on Nov 19 and raised its outlook. On Friday Gap shares were up about 14.6% by late morning after Q3 net sales of $4.0bn, up 2%.

items.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv; Poland reports airspace violation
items.summary: Russia carried out overnight strikes on Kyiv and other regions, with Ukrainian officials reporting deaths and dozens injured; casualty figures differ between reports. Poland's defence minister said three objects, reportedly two missiles and a drone, entered Polish airspace overnight during allied exercises.

items.title: Trump joins Ukraine talks with European leaders and Zelensky
items.summary: Trump sat in on a Nov 19 meeting led by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff with European leaders and President Zelensky and said Putin wants a deal. The WSJ reports US envoys have discussed NATO membership for Ukraine as one option if it cedes territory; this has not been confirmed officially.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin say a nuclear war cannot be won
items.summary: After their trilateral meeting, the three leaders issued a joint statement committing to talks on reducing nuclear risk. Putin acknowledged the statement does not set ambitious targets.

items.title: Senate blocks Iran war powers measure, 51–48
items.summary: Senate Republicans voted down a resolution that would have ended US involvement in the Iran war or required congressional approval; the House passed it in September. Trump told Axios he will not decide next steps on Iran until after the new year.

items.title: World Court finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9–6 on Nov 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. Myanmar rejected the ruling; the UK ordered the expulsion of Myanmar's defence attaché.

items.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy permitting bill
items.summary: The bill shortens federal environmental review and litigation timelines for energy and infrastructure projects. Critics say it weakens environmental and tribal protections.

items.title: Hungary expected to lift veto on Ukraine's last EU clusters
items.summary: Diplomats told Euronews Hungary would drop its objection to opening Ukraine's final two accession negotiating clusters at an EU ambassadors' meeting on Nov 20, allowing Ukraine and Moldova to open all clusters. The vote had not taken place at publication.

items.title: Texans beat Colts 26–3, move to 4–6
items.summary: C.J. Stroud went 21 of 27 for 194 yards and three TDs and David Montgomery ran for 107 yards on Thursday night; Will Anderson Jr. added a sack and a safety. Houston is second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–2) and hosts Baltimore on Sunday, Nov 29 at 12:00 PM CT.

items.title: Broncos (7–2) host Raiders Sunday, 3:25 PM CT
items.summary: Denver, tied with Kansas City (7–2) atop the AFC West, plays Las Vegas (4–6) at Empower Field on Sunday, Nov 22 at 3:25 PM CT on CBS. On Wednesday's report WR Jaylen Waddle and CB Riley Moss (concussions) were full participants and S Brandon Jones (hamstring) was limited.

items.title: ATP Finals: Shelton reaches first semifinal; Zverev finishes 3–0
items.summary: On Thursday Ben Shelton beat Rafael Jodar 7-6(8), 7-5 to take second place in the McEnroe Group, and Alexander Zverev defeated Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6) to win it unbeaten. Shelton is due to face Carlos Alcaraz in the semifinals.

items.title: ATP Finals: Medvedev–Tiafoe decides last semifinal spot Friday
items.summary: Friday's Lendl Group matches are Alcaraz vs Flavio Cobolli and Daniil Medvedev vs Frances Tiafoe, with the Medvedev–Tiafoe winner taking the final semifinal place. Alcaraz beat Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 on Wednesday.
